newsitem.title: FRANCE: No deadline, no sole option on Cr Foncier -Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: No deadline, no sole option on Cr Foncier -Arthuis.

text.p: Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday he was not doggedly set on a sole option for dealing with French bank Credit Foncier but Credit Immobilier was the only one in the frame for a bank which would not survive alone.

"We are not trying to shut ourselves into any tight calendar or one sole option, but we're saying the taxpayer is not the right answer," Arthuis, who was questioned in the Senate as a staff sit-in at Credit Foncier dragged through day seven.
"So far only one partner has come forward, that is Credit Immobilier. And it's with (Credit Immobilier) that there should be an effort to find a solution," he said.
"If another partner were to present itself, the government would clearly listen, the door is open," he said.

Arthuis announced plans in July for cooperatively run Credit Immobilier to take over the home loans business of Credit Foncier and for the rest of the bank to be spun off into a state holding company to be wound down over time.

Government-appointed mediator Philippe Rouvillois was meeting unions from 1430 GMT and Arthuis said he hoped Rouvillois would be able to assess whether a prediction of a profit of one billion francs for 1996 contained elements that would recur in the following years.
